lines.text: Alicia: Where did you go on your holiday?
Fabio: I took a bus across America from New York to San Francisco.
It took 18 days and it was so interesting.
Alicia: Wasn’t it boring on the bus?
Fabio: No.
We didn’t stay on the bus all the time.
We went to two national parks, Yosemite and the Grand Canyon.
I think Yosemite was better than the Grand Canyon because there were fewer people.
There were over 500 when I was at the Grand Canyon.
There’s a bridge made of glass and you can stand on it and look down at the river.
I know it’s not dangerous, but I felt uncomfortable standing on it and didn’t really like it.
Alicia: Was it hot?
Fabio: Yes, but it rained, too.
I didn’t like that.
But Yosemite Park was amazing.
There were lots of trees so it was very green and not too hot.
I loved it there.
Alicia: Where did you go next?
Fabio: To San Francisco.
You should go there – it has lots of unusual shops and fantastic food.
One pizza restaurant made 30 different kinds of pizza and they weren’t like the fast food pizzas we get here.
More like the ones my grandmother cooked at home.
Alicia: Did you stay in a hotel?
Fabio: Yes, in San Francisco we did.
It was cheap and small – there were only six rooms and the other people staying there were nice.
The city is amazing!
I think you should visit, too.
You’d love it!

lines.text: Fahd: Hi Haru.
I hear you have a new job.
Haru: Yes, I’m going to work as a ranger.
Fahd: What’s that?
Haru: It’s a person who helps care for nature.
Fahd: So you help animals?
Haru: Not really, although I have to make sure the places they live in are safe.
It’s my dream job and that’s why I went to university.
There is one problem though.
Fahd: What’s that?
Haru: Well it’s in the countryside so I have to leave my hometown.
I’m not sure I want to do that.
Fahd: Where is the job?
Haru: In Terwick.
It’s more than 100 kilometres away, so I have to move and live on my own.
Fahd: Do you have to find somewhere to live?
Haru: No, one of the good things about this job is that it has a cabin.
Fahd: What’s that?
Is it like a stone house?
Haru: No, it’s a small wooden house that I can live in while I work for the company.
When I leave, I have to find another place to live.
Fahd: Is the money good?
Haru: It’s OK, but not great.
I will earn enough to buy all my food, but I don’t think I can afford to go out very much, or come home often.
I think I’ll be very busy, so I won’t have much free time.
Fahd: Do you think you’ll be lonely?
You won’t have any friends there.
Haru: I know, but I enjoy being alone, too.
Fahd: Well, we can all come and visit you in the holidays.
Haru: That would be great!

lines.text: Teacher: OK, today I want you to tell the class about your family at home.
Marius, do you have a brother or sister?
Marius: Yes, I have a brother.
He’s 14 and he loves football and basketball and he goes to the gym on Saturday mornings with our father.
They both love to exercise, but I don’t.
I like to play computer games.
Teacher: Yes, we know you do.
What about you Clara?
Clara: I have a big sister and a little brother.
My sister Katia likes school.
She does her homework after school and then she reads books about science.
She wants to study Science at university.
My brother is five years old and watches TV every evening after school.
Teacher: Sofía, do you have a brother?
Sofía: No, I have one sister, Rosa.
She’s 23 and lives in Mexico with my grandparents.
She’s at university in Mexico City.
Rosa wants to be a doctor and work in a hospital.
She goes online and chats to my mother every evening, but she’s very busy so they don’t chat for a long time.
Teacher: And Jason?
What about your family?
Jason: My parents live in Beijing in China.
My father is a chef and he works in a restaurant in the city centre.
My mother is a school teacher.
They are both very busy, but my mother texts me every day.
Marius: Do you have any brothers or sisters, Jason?
Jason: No, I don’t.

lines.text: Nour: I live in Cairo in Egypt.
Cairo is a very busy city with many people.
The River Nile is in Cairo and there are many bridges over the river, but a very famous bridge is the Qasr El Nil Bridge.
Cairo has many old buildings and also lots of new buildings.
There is a university near the river and many shopping centres, hotels and beautiful parks.
At weekends I go with my family to a park next to a big hotel and relax all afternoon.
The weather in Cairo is very hot and dry in the summer and there are sand storms that come from the desert.
In the winter it rains a little, but it is still hot.
Peter: My hometown is in Switzerland.
It is small, beautiful and very busy.
In the winter we have a lot of snow and it is very cold, but the sky is blue and it is sunny.
The summer in the mountains isn’t very hot and it rains, but the forests are green.
Lots of people come to my town and walk in the mountains or ski in the snow.
The town has two hotels, a lot of restaurants and a train station.
We also have a supermarket and a park with an old monument in it.
Next to the park is a library and there is a little café behind it.
I go there every Saturday to have coffee.

lines.text: Kenji: Hi Sophia, is that a photo of your family?
Sophia: Yes.
Here, look.
Kenji: Are these your parents?
Sophia: Yes, my mother Hannah and my father Marco.
Kenji: Where are they from?
Sophia: Well, my father is from Italy, but my mother isn’t.
She’s from Australia.
Kenji: So your grandparents are Australian?
Sophia My grandmother isn’t.
She’s from England, but she lives in Melbourne with my grandfather.
Kenji: But is your father Italian?
Sophia: Yes, he is.
My brother and I are, too.
My father’s a TV presenter in Rome and my mother’s a writer.
She’s very creative.
She writes children’s books.
Kenji: Is your brother a student at university?
Sophia: Yes, he’s a student, he wants to be a scientist and work in America.
What about your family, Kenji?
Kenji: Here’s a photo of my parents, my brother and my two sisters.
Sophia: Where is your family from?
Kenji: We come from Tokyo in Japan, but my brother and I don’t live there now.
I’m a student here and my brother works in England, in London.
Sophia: What does he do?
Kenji: He’s a teacher and my sister Yumiko is a manager in a hotel in Tokyo.
My other sister is 15 and still at school, but she wants to be a chef.
Sophia: And you?
What do you want to do?
Kenji: I want to be a businessman.
I want to work in China or the UAE.
And what do you want to do in the future?
Sophia: I don’t know.
Not a businesswoman though.
Maybe a doctor like my grandfather.

There is a big desert with a lot of sand, but no trees.

lines.text: Matt: Welcome to Renton and I hope you enjoy your stay here.
I’m going to give you some directions so you can find your way around while you are here.
We’re outside the train station now and in front of us is a historical monument.
You can enjoy the sun in our lovely park.
It’s behind the small shopping centre next to the café.
There are lots of trees and flowers and a very old fountain in the middle.
There is a food court in the shopping centre and you can buy your food here.
As you can see there is a department store opposite the station.
Liz: Where’s the bank?
Matt: The bank is next to the library.
Go down Wood Street, past the museum, turn right and the bank is between the library and the cinema.
Alice: Where’s the university?
Matt: That’s over the river.
Walk down Ship Street, next to the shopping centre.
You can see the river at the end of the street and a bridge to the right.
Go over the bridge and the university campus is in front of you.
I have maps of the town with me or you can download the app.
Renton is a beautiful town and it’s very safe, too.
I hope you enjoy your time here.
Thank you.

lines.text: Good afternoon everyone, thank you for coming.
My name is Karen Smith and I’m here from The Future Advice Centre.
Next year you finish school so it’s time to think about what you want to do next.
There are some important things for you to think about and today we’re going to talk about jobs and – for those of you who want to go to university – choosing a subject to study.
The first thing you need to ask yourself is – do I want to leave school next year, or do I want to go to university?
You don’t have to go to university.
If you want to work in a restaurant, I think it’s better to work and learn at the same time.
A chef can teach you how to cook and you get good experience.
Another thing to remember is that the job doesn’t have to pay very well.
Choose a job you enjoy.
Many creative people like musicians don’t earn much, but they often have fun.
Do you want a job where you help people, for example as a doctor or nurse?
They work long hours, but their jobs are interesting.
Whatever job you do you should have time to relax and enjoy your life.
It’s good to see friends and watch TV.
You should talk to your parents, too.
They can also give you advice about jobs but remember it’s your life and your future.

lines.text: Teacher: So last week we had an international food festival with food from fifteen different countries.
Did you all enjoy it?
Antonio: Yes, it was great.
I read that two hundred people came to the college to try our food.
I ate home-cooked Japanese food for the first time.
It’s very different to Mexican food.
In Mexico we eat a lot of tacos and rice.
My mum cooks healthy meals, but I often eat burgers because it’s quicker.
Rosa: It’s the same in Italy, at home we eat pasta with meat and vegetables, but when I go out, I eat pizza with chips.
Did you know that people bought sixty-two pizzas at the festival?
It was the most popular dish.
Teacher: Wow, that’s a lot of pizzas!
What dish did you bring to the festival, Da-hyun?
Da-hyun: My favourite – noodles with fish and vegetables.
It’s very popular in Korea.
I ate tacos and rice at the festival.
The price was good, it only cost three dollars.
Teacher: I didn’t have a taco, but I had meat and salad.
It was seven dollars, so more expensive than your taco, but it was delicious and better than the sandwich I usually have from the campus café.
Antonio: The food at college isn’t very nice, only the chips are OK.
Teacher: True, maybe we should have more food festivals, so we can eat better food.
The college made nearly two thousand dollars, one thousand eight hundred to be exact, so they definitely think it was a good idea.

lines.text: David: I want to drive into London next week – my brother lives there, but I read that I have to pay a congestion charge.
What’s that?
Amy: That’s the money you have to pay to drive into the centre of the city on weekdays.
Why don’t you take the metro or a bus into the centre?
There’s a lot of traffic in London and there are bus lanes everywhere.
David: Are they the parts of the road only for buses?
Amy: Yes and no.
They help the buses move around the city faster, but taxis and motorbikes can also go in them.
However, cars are not allowed during the day.
The passengers think bus lanes are a good idea because their journeys are much quicker, but don’t drive in a bus lane or you’ll get a fine.
David: What’s a fine?
Amy: It’s money you pay when you do something wrong.
It’s about £80, but you only pay £40 if you pay within two weeks.
David: Oh, no.
I don’t think I want to drive into London.
Amy: Most people travel by public transport.
David: Is it expensive?
Amy: The metro fares are cheap.
The fare means the price of the ticket.
David: So how much is it?
Amy: When are you going?
David: Tuesday morning.
Amy: Don’t go at peak time.
That’s the time when a lot of people travel.
David: Well, I have to leave at 8:30.
Amy: Where does your brother live?
David: He lives in central London.
Amy: That’s zone 1.
So you certainly don’t want to drive into the centre.
Park your car in the suburbs and then take the metro.
David: The suburbs?
What are they?
Amy: Oh, the suburbs are areas outside the city or town centre.
That’s where most people live.
Drive your car to a metro station, park and take the metro.
It’s much easier!
David: OK, I’ll do that.
